CITY COUNCIL
  NOTICE AND AGENDA FOR SPECIAL MEETING

UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF

WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY
ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM
MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

Council beginning at 6 p.m. on December 13, 2022 in the Council Chambers at Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
Boulevard, and via video conference. Speakers at this meeting are limited to speak only on the items listed on the
following agenda:

less than 24-hours before the start of the meeting and delivered to each member of the Norwalk City Council and to
the following newspapers: Herald American, Cerritos Community News, Norwalk Patriot, and Whittier Daily News, all

Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. 22-70 – RESULTS OF THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL
  ELECTION HELD NOVEMBER 8, 2022

Background:

On June 7, 2022 City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-25 calling and giving notice of
the November 8, 2022 consolidated election with Los Angeles County to elect two
members to the City Council for full terms of four years. There were a total of five
individuals who qualified to run for the two four-year seats.

The County of Los Angeles has completed the canvass of the results and the appropriate
Resolution has been prepared for adoption. The results are attached as Exhibit “A” to
Resolution No. 22-70. The total number of ballots cast in this election were 18,887,
equating to 33% of the registered voters. Seventy-nine percent of the ballots cast were
by Vote-By-Mail.

The election results declare that Tony Ayala and Jennifer Perez were re-elected to the
Norwalk City Council for four-year terms.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:
Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-70, A RESOLUTION OF THE
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK RECITING THE FACT OF THE
GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD ON NOVEMBER 8, 2022, DECLARING THE
RESULTS AND SUCH OTHER MATTERS AS PROVIDED BY LAW.
Attachment:

Resolution No. 22-70

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

SUBJECT: CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

Background:

Annually, City Council selects one of its members to serve as Mayor and one to serve as
Vice Mayor. Following is the procedure for reorganization:

1.  The City Clerk will declare that the next item of business shall be the selection of a
  Mayor and a Vice Mayor for the upcoming year.

2.  The City Clerk declares that nominations are in order for the office of Mayor. The
  City Clerk accepts nominations; a second to the nomination is not necessary. If
  there are no further nominations, the City Clerk will close the nominations and take
  a roll call vote. If more than one nomination, a vote will be taken in the order of the
  nomination. Following the vote(s), the City Clerk declares the Mayor elected.

3.  The newly elected Mayor will preside over the election of the Vice Mayor in the
  same manner as outlined for the Mayor and conduct the remainder of the meeting.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council turn the meeting over to the City Clerk to initiate the
process for the selection of the Mayor and Vice Mayor.
   City Council Agenda Report
  December 13, 2022

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

SUBJECT: APPOINTMENT OF TRUSTEE - GREATER LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT

Background:

The Board of Directors for the Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District
(District) is comprised of representatives from cities that are serviced by the District.
Pursuant to Section 2022 of the State Health and Safety Code (Code), City Council has
the authority to “make an appointment of a person who shall be a voter in that city and a
resident of that portion of the city that is within the district.”

The City Council has historically appointed one of its members to serve as a trustee on
the District. Vice Mayor Valencia was appointed to a two-year term in 2020, which expires
January 1, 2023. Therefore, there is a need to either re-appoint Vice Mayor Valencia or
appoint another member for a two- or four-year term. Members serve for the entire term
unless they resign.

According to the Code, Vice Mayor Valencia may be reappointed for a two- or four-year
term or a new person may be appointed. The Board of Directors meets the second
Thursday of each month at 7:00 p.m.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council appoint a member to serve as a trustee on the Greater
Los Angeles County Vector Control District for a two- or four-year term.

Attachments: N/A
   City Council Agenda Report
  December 13, 2022

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

SUBJECT: PLANNING COMMISSION APPOINTMENTS

Background:

Section 2.16.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code provides that the terms of the members
of the Norwalk Planning Commission shall be coexistent with that of the City
Councilmember making the appointment. As Councilmembers Ayala and Perez were re-
elected, they may either re-appoint their current commissioners or choose new
representatives.

The Office of the City Clerk has posted the mandatory vacancy notice in order to allow
appointments to be made at this meeting. The next meeting of the Planning Commission
is scheduled for December 14. New appointments are needed to allow the Commission
to continue to function.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: Terms of office posted.

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends Councilmembers Ayala and Perez appoint members of the community
to serve as Planning Commissioners for four-year terms.

Attachments: None
